QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_41

question.text: Under Regulation 29, an AIF can be wound up in all of the following circumstances EXCEPT:

answer.text: Tenure of the AIF or its schemes (as per PPM) is over
Trustees' opinion that winding-up is in interests of investors
75% of investors by value pass a resolution to wind up
25% of investors by value opt for redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 29 lists four winding-up grounds: (a) tenure expiry, (b) trustee opinion, (c) 75%-by-value investor resolution, (d) SEBI direction. Option D — a 25% redemption request — is NOT a winding-up ground for close-ended AIF. For open-ended, redemptions are processed subject to gates/locks, but they do not trigger winding-up. The Trap: Options A, B, C are three of the four PDF grounds. The trap is the 25% number (which is the bid-value floor for in-specie, NOT a winding trigger). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D test the same Regulation 29 grounds. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat III open-ended schemes don't 'wind up' on redemption pressure — they close-to-new-subs, gate, side-pocket, or suspend. Winding-up under Reg 29 is a tail event requiring 75%-by-value consent or a trustee/SEBI trigger.
